inventory.anchor: include of nr_stealth_proxy_udp.h; NrSocket::create (UDP: the proxy layer); NrSocketBase::CreateSocket (the config to NrSocket; no UDP socket of a PeerConnection in a content process)
evidence: +// STEALTH-HOOK(fingerprint/webrtc/declared-network): the declared host sockets of this process (R3). Every NrSocket
inventory.notes: The rule of the UDP of a PeerConnection, made where its socket is born: no proxy = a plain socket, SOCKS5 = the SOCKS5 UDP layer, a proxy without UDP = a socket whose datagrams go nowhere. In a content process the UDP sockets of a PeerConnection are refused (they would go out direct). Also (feature webrtc-declared-network, fingerprint/webrtc/declared-network): a host UDP socket of a declared address binds the wildcard of its family on the port of its connection and reports the declared address with that port; a datagram between two sockets of this process goes on the kernel's loopback while each end sees the other's declared address (StealthOwnPorts).
